newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-DKB chairman indicted in racketeer scandal.
newsitem.headline: Ex-DKB chairman indicted in racketeer scandal.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors said on Friday they had indicted former chairman of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) Tadashi Okuda for extending 11.78 billion yen ($100 million) in loans to "sokaiya" corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike.
Prosecutors said Okuda had extended the loans to Koike from DKB through Tokyo-based financial firm Daiwa Shinyo in about 52 installments between July 7, 1994, and September 6, 1996.

Okuda is the latest in a series of former executives from DKB and leading Japanese brokerage Nomura Securities Co Ltd to be indicted in a high-profile racketeer pay-off scandal, which is unfolding just as Japan begins "Big Bang" reforms of its financial sector.

Earlier on Friday, Japan's Finance Ministry filed a complaint with Tokyo prosecutors against DKB and several former DKB executives for allegedly violating the Banking Law by hiding information about loans to the sokaiya racketeer from ministry investigators.
Finance Ministry officials are expected to unveil administrative penalties against Nomura, and possibly DKB as well, next week.

Payoffs to sokaiya -- corporate racketeers who buy shares in companies and try to extort money by threatening to expose dubious business practices, or who are sometimes employed by firms to quash questions from legitimate shareholders at annual meetings -- have been illegal since 1983. But many Japanese companies have found it difficult to cut the ties that bind them to the underworld. ($1=117 yen)
